title: User-centric Subjective Leaderboard by Customizable Reward Modeling
reasoning: The paper focuses on building a customizable reward model and leaderboard (USL) for evaluating LLMs based on subjective user preferences regarding style, tone, and content structure. While it mentions 'ethical' as one of many possible content criteria extracted from user data, it does not evaluate or benchmark religion, morals, or ethics as a primary component of the work.
